mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (< -0.2) between GDPC1 YoY declines > 2% and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6.5% for two months in a row.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which elevates input costs and reduces profit expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (< -0.2) between INDPRO contraction events and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 5-year moving average by more than 10% for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when HOUST exceeds its 5-year moving average by more than 10% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month moving averages indicates a labor market expansion with falling unemployment, which boosts consumer purchasing power and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (< -0.2) between RSAFS < 12-month MA for six months and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests.
